turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Hello everyone. Can you all hear me okay?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Yes, loud and clear, Camille.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I can hear you. Ingrid, are you with us? I only see your initials.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: I'm here, sorry. My camera's decided not to work this morning.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: That's fine, Ingrid, we don't need to see you to talk about money. So this is the budget review for the third quarter. Priyanka, you sent the spreadsheet last night, do you want to walk us through it?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Sure. The short version is that we're over by about a hundred and twenty thousand euros for the quarter, and almost all of it comes from two lines. The first is hosting. Nimbus put their prices up at the start of the summer and nobody renegotiated, so we've paid the new rate for three months. The second is travel, which I've started calling the Okonkwo line.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Which was worth every cent, by the way.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I'm not saying it wasn't. I'm saying it's on the line.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay. How much is Nimbus on its own, Priyanka?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Roughly seventy thousand over plan. Travel is about forty, and the rest is small stuff.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Can I jump in on Nimbus? Because that number isn't only the price increase.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Go ahead, Ingrid.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: So about half of it is the price, yes. The other half is us. We moved the reporting jobs onto bigger machines in August because the nightly runs were too slow, and Kwabena warned me it would cost more. We just never put a number on it. That's on operations, I'll own that.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Thanks for being straight about it. Has Kwabena given you an estimate since?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Last week, yes. He thinks we can bring the bill down by about thirty percent if we move the reporting jobs back to smaller machines and start them a bit earlier.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Thirty percent of the whole Nimbus bill, or of the overrun?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Of the whole bill.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Oh. That's a lot more than I expected.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Okay, but before we start cutting things, I want to say something about travel, because I can see where this is going.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Go on, Bartholomew.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Quillfeather is the biggest deal we've had in two years. We've been to their office five times since June, and every visit moved it forward. They're ready to sign for three years, around four hundred thousand euros a year. If we stop the trips now, right before the contract, we send exactly the wrong message. I don't want to be the one telling them we can't come anymore because of a spreadsheet.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Nobody's asking you to tell Quillfeather anything, Bartholomew.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Then what are we asking?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Whether five visits in one quarter is normal, and whether every visit needed four people on the plane.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: It needed the right people. Their finance director wanted to meet our product team, not just me.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Could some of those meetings have been on video?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Some of them, sure, but not the signing, Ingrid. You don't sign a deal that size on a video call.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay, let me stop us for a second. Nobody here thinks the Quillfeather trips were a mistake. Bartholomew, I want that deal signed. But Priyanka's right that the money has to come from somewhere, and I'd rather decide it today than have the same argument next quarter.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Fair enough.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Priyanka, what do you suggest?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Two things. First, we freeze travel for the rest of the year at what's left, which is about fifteen thousand euros, and anything above that goes to Camille for approval. Second, operations delivers the savings Kwabena found, and we renegotiate the Nimbus contract before it renews in December.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Fifteen thousand won't cover the signing trip and the kickoff.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: How much would?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Um, twenty-five, maybe thirty.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: That's double.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: It's double of a very small number, Priyanka.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Can I suggest something?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Sorry, go ahead, Ingrid.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: If Kwabena's change goes in next month, we save something like fifteen thousand a month on Nimbus. That alone covers the extra for Bartholomew's trips, and then some. So we don't have to pick one or the other, as long as the savings are real.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: As long as they're real. That's my whole job, Ingrid, checking that they're real.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Ingrid Haugland, always the peacemaker.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay, I like that. So here's my proposal. Travel gets twenty-five thousand for the rest of the year, not thirty, and Bartholomew, anything above that comes to me with a reason. Can you live with that?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Twenty-five works, Camille. I'll make it work.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Ingrid, you own the Nimbus savings. Can you and Kwabena have the smaller machines running by the end of next month?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: End of next month is fine. I'll check with Kwabena Mensah today, but I don't see a problem.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: And I'll need the real numbers every month, not estimates.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: You'll have them on the first Monday of every month.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Priyanka, can you lead the Nimbus renegotiation? You know that contract better than anyone.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Yes, but I want someone from operations in the room. I can read a contract, I can't tell them how many machines we need.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: I'll come. Or I'll send Kwabena, he knows the details better than I do.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Good. Bartholomew, last question. When do you honestly think Quillfeather signs?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: End of November. Their legal team has the contract, and they usually take three or four weeks.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: So that revenue lands next quarter, not this one.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Then, Priyanka, keep it out of the forecast until it's actually signed. I don't want to plan on money we don't have.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: That's a bit pessimistic, Camille.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: It is. I'd rather be pleasantly surprised.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Fine. But when it signs, I'm expecting a very nice dinner.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Within budget, Bartholomew.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Of course.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Let me recap so we all leave with the same list. Travel is capped at twenty-five thousand euros until the end of the year, and anything above comes to me. Ingrid and Kwabena move the reporting jobs to smaller machines by the end of next month, and Ingrid sends Priyanka the real Nimbus numbers every month. Priyanka leads the Nimbus renegotiation before December, with Ingrid or Kwabena in the room. Quillfeather stays out of the forecast until it's signed. Did I miss anything?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Only that I'll send the updated spreadsheet by Thursday, so everyone can check the numbers.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Perfect, thanks, Priyanka.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Nothing from me.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: All good on my side.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Great. Thanks, everyone, and good luck with Quillfeather, Bartholomew.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Thanks, Camille. Talk soon.
